questions.question: Discuss the major methods of Costing and explain their applicability in different business situations. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html: • Major methods of costing and their applicability Costing methods are selected according to the nature of production, the product or service, and how costs can be identified. The major methods are: Method Meaning / application Typical example Unit / output costing Cost per unit is determined where output is homogeneous and continuous. Cement, bricks, sugar, paper Job costing Costs are accumulated separately for each specific job or customer Printing, repair workshops, custom furniture order. Batch costing A batch is treated as a cost unit; batch cost is divided by units in the batch. Pharmaceuticals, garments, components Contract costing Costs are collected for each large, long-term contract, often at a site. Buildings, roads, bridges, shipbuilding Process costing Costs are accumulated process- wise for continuous, repetitive production; average cost per process/unit is found. Chemicals, oil refining, textiles Operation costing Costs are accumulated for a defined operation or series of operations, often for standardised components. Engineering and component manufacture Operating / service costing Cost per service unit is calculated for service organisations. Transport per passenger-km, hospitals per patient-day, hotels per room-day Multiple / composite costing Two or more methods are combined when a product has many components or stages. Cars, machinery, complex equipment

questions.question: A publishing house purchases 60,000 units of a particular item of material per year at a unit cost of Rs. 40 each. The following further data are available: Annual return on investment: 12% Rent, insurance and tax per unit per annum: Rs. 8 Cost of placing an order: Rs. 120 Determine: (1) EOQ, (2) Frequency of orders in terms of days / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) and frequency of orders (Value Liberally)
  • Annual demand (A) = 60,000 units;
  • Ordering cost per order (O) = 120;
  • Unit price = 40;
  • Return on investment = 12%;
  • other carrying charges = 8 per unit per annum.
  • Annual carrying cost per unit (C) = 12% of 40 + 8 = 4.80 + 8 = 12.80.
  • EOQ = √(2AO/C).
  • EOQ = √[(2 × 60,000 × 120) ÷ 12.80] = √1,125,000 = 1,060.66 units, (1,061 units.)
  • Number of orders per year = 60,000 ÷ 1,060.66 = 56.57 orders.
  • Frequency in days (using a 365-day year) = 365 ÷ 56.57 = 6.45 days between orders.

questions.question: Define Labour Turnover and explain its significance in cost accounting. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Labour turnover and its significance in cost accounting
  • Labour turnover is the rate at which employees leave an organisation and are replaced during a specified
  • period. It indicates the extent of labour movement in and out of the organisation.
  • Common measurement methods:
  • • Separation method = (Number of separations during the period ÷ Average number of workers) × 100.
  • • Replacement method = (Number of replacements during the period ÷ Avg. number of workers) × 100.
  • • Flux method = [(Separations + Replacements) ÷ Average number of workers] × 100.
  • Average number of workers is commonly calculated as (Opening workers + Closing workers) ÷ 2, unless
  • monthly averages are available.
  • Significance: (1) high turnover increases recruitment, selection and training costs; (2) inexperienced
  • workers may cause lower output and more defects; (3) production schedules can be disrupted; (4)
  • overtime and replacement costs may rise; (5) it helps management assess labour stability, morale and
  • working conditions;
  • A moderate turnover due to normal retirement or movement may be unavoidable; the reasons should be
  • analysed rather than interpreting the percentage in isolation.

questions.question: A company has three production departments and two service departments and for a period the departmental distribution summary has the following totals: Production Departments Service Departments P1 P2 P3 S1 S2 Total Overheads (Rs) 800 700 500 234 300 The expenses of the service departments are charged out on a percentage basis as follows: A B C5 X Y S1 Deptt 20% 40% 30% --- 10% S2 Deptt 40% 20% 20% 20% --- Prepare a statement showing the apportionment of two service departments expenses to production departments by Simultaneous Equation Method. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Apportionment of service department overheads by simultaneous equation method
  • Overhead cost as per primary Distribution Summary:
  • P1 = 800, P2 = 700, P3 = 500, S1 = 234, S2 = 300.
  • The allocation percentages in the paper are interpreted as follows:
  • P1 P2 P3 S1 S2
  • S1 20% 40% 30% 10%
  • S2 40% 20% 20% 20%
  • (1) Calculation of total overheads of Service departments
  • Let total cost of Service dept... S1 be X and total cost of S2 be Y
  • x = 234 + 20% of y = 234 + 0.20y
  • y = 300 + 10% of x = 300 + 0.10x
  • Substitute y into the first equation: X= 234 + 0.20(300 + 0.10x) = 234 + 60 + 0.02x.
  • Therefore 0.98x = 294, and X = 300. Then Y = 300 + 0.10(300) = 330.
  • Overheads of S1 dept. =X= 300
  • Overheads of S2 dept. =Y= 330
  • (2) Overheads Chargeable to Production departments
  • Over heads of S1 dept. = 300
  • Less overhead Chargeable to S2 Dept. = 30 (300*10/100)
  • = 300-30=270
  • Over heads of S2 dept. = 330
  • Less overhead Chargeable to S2 Dept. = 66 (330*20/100)
  • = 330-66=264
  • (3) Statement showing secondary Distribution
  • Particulars Ratio P1 P2 P3
  • Overheads as per Primary
  • Distribution ------ 800 700 500
  • Share from S1 (270) (2:4:3) 60 120 90
  • Share from S2 (264) (4:2:2) 132 66 66
  • Total Overheads 992 886 656

questions.question: The standard time for a job is 12 hours and the wage rate is ₹80 per hour. A worker completes the job in 9 hours. Calculate his earnings under (a) Halsey Bonus Plan (50%), (b) Halsey-Weir Premium Plan, and (c) Rowan Plan. Compare the earnings under the three incentive plans. / [CO3] [15x2 = 30]

• Wages under Halsey 50%, Halsey–Weir and Rowan incentive plans

  • Actual time = 9 hours;
  • Wage rate = ₹80 per hour.
  • Time saved = 12 − 9 = 3 hours.
  • Time wages for actual time = 9 × ₹80 = ₹720.
  • Standard time wages = 12 × ₹80 = ₹960.

  • Wages= (Time Taken * Rate) + 50%( Time Saved * Rate)
